subsystems.name: Legal corpus and ingestion
subsystems.role: collects statutes, case law, regulations and secondary sources into a searchable store.

subsystems.name: Retrieval engine
subsystems.role: finds the passages most relevant to a legal question.

subsystems.name: Generative drafting model
subsystems.role: produces coherent legal text such as memos, contracts or briefs.

subsystems.name: Citation verification
subsystems.role: checks that every cited authority exists and actually supports the stated proposition.

subsystems.name: Workflow and filing interface
subsystems.role: moves a document through review, signature and submission to a court or agency.

subsystems.name: Oversight and compliance
subsystems.role: keeps a human accountable and creates an auditable record.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the legal corpus
buildSteps.detail: Gather public and licensed case law, statutes, regulations and forms, then normalise them into a consistent machine-readable format.

buildSteps.title: Index for retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Split documents into passages, compute vector embeddings and build keyword and citation indexes so relevant authorities can be found quickly.

buildSteps.title: Adapt a language model
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune or prompt a large language model on legal text so it writes in the correct register and structure.

buildSteps.title: Build the retrieval-augmented pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Connect the model to the retrieval engine so every draft is grounded in retrieved sources rather than the model's memory alone.

buildSteps.title: Add citation verification
buildSteps.detail: Parse each citation, fetch the cited source and check that it exists and supports the sentence it is attached to; reject or flag drafts that fail.

buildSteps.title: Create drafting workflows
buildSteps.detail: Encode templates for common documents and assemble them from retrieved law and case facts.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with filing systems
buildSteps.detail: Connect to court e-filing portals and practice-management software so a finished draft can be submitted and tracked.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with human review
buildSteps.detail: Run the system in assisted mode, where a lawyer checks and signs off, while collecting data on errors and edge cases.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and update
buildSteps.detail: Continuously ingest new decisions and statutes, retrain or re-index, and monitor for drift and hallucination.

prerequisites.why: they provide the fluent drafting and reasoning ability that makes synthesis possible.
it grounds outputs in real sources but is not yet reliable enough for unsupervised legal work.
authoritative case law and statutes are needed for both retrieval and verification.
current methods catch many fabricated citations but not all misstatements of law.
courts and bars generally require a licensed human to sign and take responsibility for filings.

pathway.milestone: AI-assisted legal research and first-draft generation with a lawyer in the loop
pathway.unlocks: faster document preparation and reduced routine drafting time.

pathway.milestone: verified drafting for routine, high-volume matters such as simple contracts and immigration forms
autonomous research and drafting for narrow, well-bounded legal questions
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end synthesis without a lawyer for every step, if regulators allow.

pathway.milestone: autonomous filing and case management across jurisdictions
pathway.unlocks: fully automated legal services, contingent on ethics rules, liability frameworks and public trust.
